raw_case_text:
A one-year-old girl was born after a second full-term pregnancy via spontaneous vaginal delivery, weighting 3200 g. The pregnancy was complicated by dysfunction of the placenta and the threat of interruption at 11 weeks. Chronic herpes infection was diagnosed in the pregnant mother. Family history was non-contributory. Congenital heart defects (membranous ventricular septal defect [VSD] and open oval window) were confirmed on the second day of life.
At the age of 1.5 months the girl was admitted to the Department of Infectious Diseases in critical condition, with severe respiratory, cardiovascular, and neurological disturbances. Bilateral pneumonia and urinary tract infection were diagnosed. Enterococcus faecalis was revealed in urine culture. At the age of 4.5 months open oval window was confirmed and subarterial ventricular septal defect and high pulmonary hypertension were diagnosed. Increased levels of Ig G herpes virus type I-II, Ig G cytomegalovirus, Ig G Epstein-Barr virus, and Ig G rubella virus were determined. CRP was also elevated.
Palliative surgery (narrowing of the pulmonary artery) was carried out at the age of five months. During the surgery, absence of thymus was revealed. The postoperative period was complicated by prolonged hyperthermia, which required long-term use of antibiotic therapy.
Immunological studies showed low levels of cytotoxic cells (CD3+, CD56+) - 1.5% (normal range 3-8%) and slightly decreased CD4+ at 32.3% (normal 33-58%) and monocytes / macrophages (CD14) - 3.6% (normal range - 6-13%). B-lymphocytes (CD19+) were slightly increased at 36.4% (normal range - 13-35%). While percentage values of CD3+, CD8+, NK-cells, and immunoglobulins were normal, the absolute values of CD3+, CD4+, CD8+, and NK cells were moderately reduced (Table 2). NBT test was normal. FISH analysis on metaphase plates using Vysis TUPLE1 (HIRA) Spectrum Orange/LSI ARSA Specrtum Green [Abbott] confirmed the chromosome 22q11.2 deletion: ish del(22)(q11.2q11.2)(TUPLE1-).
This patient had no palate abnormalities. Characteristic facial features were very subtle. Auxological parameters were normal. At the age of one year her weight was 9000 g, body length 76 cm. Developmental disabilities were absent in this period. Serum calcium level was normal and seizures were absent (Table 1).

subjective.chief_complaint: A 1-year-old girl with congenital heart defects (membranous/subarterial VSD and patent foramen ovale) and a history of critical infantile bilateral pneumonia, Enterococcus faecalis urinary tract infection, and intraoperative athymia was evaluated for chromosome 22q11.2 deletion syndrome.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: Born at term (3,200 g) to a mother with chronic herpes infection and first-trimester threatened miscarriage/placental dysfunction, the patient was diagnosed on day 2 of life with membranous VSD and patent foramen ovale. At 1.5 months of age, she was hospitalized in critical condition with bilateral pneumonia and Enterococcus faecalis urinary tract infection; at 4.5 months, subarterial VSD and severe pulmonary hypertension were confirmed; and at 5 months, she underwent palliative pulmonary artery banding, during which complete absence of the thymus was discovered and followed by prolonged postoperative fever requiring extended antibiotic therapy.
subjective.past_medical_history: Membranous/subarterial ventricular septal defect (VSD), patent foramen ovale, and severe pulmonary hypertension status post palliative pulmonary artery banding at 5 months of age; intraoperative athymia; critical bilateral pneumonia and Enterococcus faecalis UTI at 1.5 months of age. Non-contributory family history.
subjective.review_of_systems: History of critical respiratory, cardiovascular, and neurological disturbances at 1.5 months and prolonged postoperative hyperthermia at 5 months; negative for seizures or developmental delay at 1 year of age.

objective.physical_examination: At 1 year of age: weight 9,000 g, length 76 cm (normal growth parameters), very subtle dysmorphic facial features, intact palate without clefting, and normal neurodevelopmental milestones without seizures; complete absence of the thymus noted intraoperatively at 5 months.
objective.routine_investigations: At 1.5-4.5 months: urine culture positive for Enterococcus faecalis; elevated CRP; elevated IgG antibody titers against HSV-1/2, cytomegalovirus (CMV), Epstein-Barr virus (EBV), and rubella virus. At 1 year: normal serum calcium level, normal nitroblue tetrazolium (NBT) test, and normal serum immunoglobulin levels.
objective.advanced_workup: Echocardiography confirmed membranous/subarterial VSD, patent foramen ovale, and severe pulmonary hypertension. Flow cytometric lymphocyte subset analysis showed moderately reduced absolute counts of CD3+, CD4+, CD8+, and NK cells, low percentage of cytotoxic CD3+CD56+ cells (1.5%, normal 3-8%), mildly decreased CD4+ percentage (32.3%, normal 33-58%) and CD14+ monocytes/macrophages (3.6%, normal 6-13%), and mildly increased CD19+ B-lymphocytes (36.4%, normal 13-35%). Metaphase fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH; Vysis TUPLE1/HIRA probe) confirmed a chromosome 22q11.2 microdeletion: ish del(22)(q11.2q11.2)(TUPLE1-).

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Definitive diagnosis of DiGeorge syndrome (chromosome 22q11.2 deletion syndrome, confirmed by FISH ish del(22)(q11.2q11.2)(TUPLE1-)) presenting with conotruncal/septal congenital heart defects (VSD, PFO, pulmonary hypertension), athymia with moderate T- and NK-cell lymphopenia, and infantile bilateral pneumonia and Enterococcus faecalis UTI (with past/maternally transferred IgG positivity for CMV, EBV, HSV-1/2, and rubella, and normocalcemia without cleft palate). Managed with palliative pulmonary artery banding at 5 months and long-term antimicrobial therapy.
